subject: Post-call: Private/VPC pricing & environment + budget check
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + a few clarifying questions on VPC/private pricing

Hi Elena / Tomothy —

Thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can put together an accurate private/VPC proposal for BrightWave:

Recap (from my notes):
- Primary use case: clinical summarization + patient QA (mostly conversation history + retrieval).
- Target environments: dev, staging, production (you mentioned a possible sandbox for partners).
- Compliance: SOC2 required; HSM/KMS integration desirable.

Clarifying items we need to price the Private/VPC option:
1) Expected token volumes (approx): monthly total tokens, and a typical peak-day/peak-hour delta.
2) Target unit economics: do you have a preferred cost-per-1M-tokens target or a monthly budget range for inference?
3) Environment count: confirm number of isolated VPC environments (dev/stage/prod + any partner sandboxes).
4) Support tier: interest in Standard vs Premium (24/7 with on-call vs business hours).
5) Licensing preference: annual license + committed capacity vs month-to-month consumption pricing.

If you can send ballpark numbers for (1) and (2) that would let us draft 2 pricing approaches: a) annual reserved + lower per-token unit economics or b) consumption-first pilot pricing.

Attaching a short private pricing primer (pdf) for context. I’ll loop in Rishi to scope the technical assumptions once we get volumes.

Proposed next step: if you’re comfortable, reply with rough monthly tokens and an expected $/1M-token target or monthly budget range and we’ll return two options within 48 business hours.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Attachment: redwood_private_pricing_v1.pdf (one-page pricing primer)

From: Elena Ramos <elena@brightwavehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tomothy Lee <tom@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a few clarifying questions on VPC/private pricing

Thanks Karthik — great summary. Below are the ballpark numbers from our side. I’ve attached the security questionnaire you requested (filled).

Answers:
- Estimated monthly tokens: ~50M typical; peak days up to ~85M. Typical sequence length ~300 tokens per turn (mixed retrieval + generation).
- Concurrency: expected steady concurrency ~8–12 concurrent requests, with short spikes to ~25.
- Budget/target: we’re aiming for total inference spend (hosting + software) in the $8k–$12k/month range initially. If we commit annually we could extend to $6k–$9k/month.
- Environments: 3 primary (dev/stage/prod) + 1 sandbox for a small partner (so 4 logical environments).
- Support: leaning toward Premium for the first 6 months while we ramp — coverage for escalations and a named engineer would be useful.
- Licensing: prefer annual committed model if the unit economics are competitive — open to pilot first.

Next: please send a lane-of-effort pricing sketch (annual vs pilot) and any assumptions you need Rishi to validate. Also we’ll need SOC2 summary and k/v cache info for our security team.

Best,
Elena Ramos
VP Product Operations | BrightWave Health
elena@brightwavehealth.com

Attachment: brightwave_security_qs_filled.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a few clarifying questions on VPC/private pricing

Elena — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Two quick clarifications before we build the pricing lanes:
1) When you say 50M tokens/month typical with 300-token sequences, do you mean 50M output tokens or 50M total (prompt+output)? If unsure, assume total.
2) For the sandbox, do you want network-isolated VPC or a logically separated namespace within the same VPC? Network isolation increases infrastructure and license cost.

Plan: Rishi — can you review the sequence lengths/concurrency and flag any adjustments to kernel/throughput assumptions? I’ll draft two lanes:
- Annual committed (12-month): discounted license + lower per-1M-token charge; recommended for BrightWave if you want predictability.
- Pilot (30-day): month-to-month pricing with slightly higher per-1M-token rate and option to convert credit to committed capacity.

Elena — we’ll include an add-on line for Premium support and an environment add-on per additional VPC. Also attaching a SOC2 summary (pdf) for your security team.

Karthik

Attachment: soc2-type2-summary.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@brightwavehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-02T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a few clarifying questions on VPC/private pricing

Hi Elena — quick technical notes from a unit-econ perspective:
- If the 50M number is total tokens (prompt + gen), with average sequence length ~300 tokens and your concurrency profile, we can likely support that on a 1–2 GPU private pool with batching and prefix caching, depending on latency targets.
- Batching + KV cache should reduce effective per-token cost for repeated context; if your workflows reuse context (summaries + retrieval) we should model a 20–30% effective token reduction.
- For spikes (to 85M/day), we recommend a burst policy (short-term capacity increase) or a hybrid model where some traffic falls back to hosted instances. Both are doable; cost differs materially.

Reqs to finalize unit economics:
- Sample request distribution (ratio of short vs long sessions) or a small sample CSV of 48–72 hours of anonymized request logs.
- Target 95th-pct latency SLO for interactive flows.

We can run a 30-day pilot on a small reserved footprint to gather real telemetry and then refine the committed offer. Happy to jump on a tech call if you want to go deeper.

—Rishi
Applied ML / Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ramos <elena@brightwavehealth.com>

We’re fine with a 30-day pilot on a small reserved footprint to gather telemetry. Please include an option to convert pilot credits to an annual commitment in the quote. Also attaching a signed quick NDA (via DocuSign) and the DocuSign link for the quote when ready.

- Draft two pricing lanes (Karthik): annual committed + pilot conversion terms; include per-1M-token targets based on a 20–30% effective token reduction from caching as Rishi noted.
- Technical assumptions (Rishi): prepare pilot footprint sizing (GPU count), expected latency at 8–12 concurrency, and burst policy cost estimate for 85M/day spikes.
- Security handoff (Marissa): send SOC2 artifacts and HSM/KMS integration notes to BrightWave security contact; confirm any additional evidence needed from the drive link.
- Legal/Contract (Marissa): prepare a short pilot SOW and a convertibility clause for credits -> annual commit.

Timeline: aim to have a formal pilot quote and pilot SOW to Elena by EOD Tuesday (2026-04-07).

Karthik
